title: Moderate Campaign For Administrative Reforms
definition: The systematic and constitutional demands raised by early Indian nationalists (Moderates) between 1885 and 1905 to democratize, Indianize, and reform the British bureaucratic machinery in India.
importanceInUpsc: Crucial for understanding the evolution of Indian nationalism, early constitutional agitation, and the critique of British colonial administration. Frequently tested in Prelims regarding specific demands and in Mains GS-1 regarding the Moderate phase.
learningOutcomes: Master foundational concepts and mechanisms of the Moderate Campaign For Administrative Reforms.
Evaluate spatial distribution, institutional frameworks, and policy dimensions of early nationalist petitions.
Apply high-yield mnemonics to solve tricky Prelims and Mains questions regarding Moderate demands.
